mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand and economic expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in downturn periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% over a 3-month period, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% over the same period, signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in strong labor market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), signals disinflationary pressure without monetary tightening, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real income rises.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS stable or decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns in disinflationary periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period, coupled with a stable or decreasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), signals real economic growth without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and CPIAUCSL stable or decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of real growth without inflation are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
